history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: CSV row 2307 is a confirmed duplicate of seq 1013 (id sri-ranganayaka-swamy-temple-srirangapur); seq 1015 is yet another duplicate record of the same shrine - keep/drop decision needed. The Sri Ranganayaka Swamy Temple at Srirangapuram village (Pebbair mandal) was built in the 18th century CE by Raja Baheri Gopal Rao of the Wanaparthy Samasthanam (Motati Reddy Vamsa), with a tank called Ranga Samudram excavated alongside and later mukha mandapas added by Sankaramba, wife of Rama Krishna Rao. It is a replica of the Sri Ranganathaswamy temple at Srirangam, earning it the name 'Uttara Srirangapuram' (the Srirangapuram of the North). Architecture is Vijayanagara style with tall gopurams, set beside the Ratna Pushkarini lake. BUILD-DATE CONFLICT (flag): epigraphical evidence gives Saka 1685 (~1763 CE); local priests claim 1540 CE - verify. CSV TOWN/DISTRICT FLAG: CSV carries the pre-2016 combined-district name 'Mahbubnagar'; the temple is at Srirangapur, Pebbair mandal, Wanaparthy district.

name: Sri Ranganayaka Swamy Temple
town_description: Srirangapur (Srirangapuram) is a village in Pebbair mandal, Wanaparthy district, Telangana, ~11 km off the Hyderabad-Bengaluru highway (NH44) and ~25 km from Wanaparthy. The temple sits on the bund of the Ratna Pushkarini lake (Ranga Samudram).

travel.airport: Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad (~120-160 km).
travel.railway: Gadwal is the nearest railway station (~40 km).
travel.road: ~10-11 km from Pebbair off NH44 (Hyderabad-Bengaluru); ~25 km from Wanaparthy; ~60 km from Kurnool; ~160 km from Hyderabad.

visitor_information.best_time: Sankranti-Kotai utsavalu and Rathotsavam season; October to March.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning 6:00 AM to 1:00 PM; evening 4:00 PM to 8:00 PM (some sources say 6 AM-8 PM straight - verify).
